text:
liam_support: FYI customer Acme Inc opened a severity-high ticket — streaming responses show p95/p99 TTFB regressions since last night's edge proxy deploy. non-stream (sync) endpoints unaffected. request IDs: req_8a7f, req_8a9b. They've seen client-side timeouts and reported UX jank.

jordan_rt: thanks — can you paste a short trace and the exact client repro? any headers (Accept: text/event-stream vs application/json)

liam_support: they said using SSE via our /v1/stream endpoint with chunking. repro steps they provided:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"long prompt...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
first byte often delayed ~800-1200ms at p95 (pre-deploy baseline ~120-180ms). total time for full response is similar to baseline.

maria_sre: logged a few of the request IDs; on the gateway we see backend start times are quick but first chunk write is delayed. stack traces show retransmits and a small burst of buffer growth in proxy out queue. attaching snip: `proxy.out_queue_ms spike = 300-900ms` for those req IDs.

amy_devex: could be coalescing heuristics changed? last deploy toggled proxy flush window to 5ms -> 20ms to reduce small-payload overheads. that would increase TTFB for streaming.

samir_engineer: confirming — change was intended to reduce tail work for many tiny chunked responses. metric we rolled up: small_write_count reduced by 18% but average flush_delay increased. Didn't think about SSE TTFB impact.

liam_support: customer needs a mitigation while we triage. they can switch to sync for now but they rely on streaming for progressive render. any quick config or client workaround?

jordan_rt: short-term: advise client to set `stream: false` OR downgrade to our dedicated edge region where proxy uses legacy flush (if they have dedicated). Also we can enable a force-flush header on their tenant: `x-rw-force-early-flush: 1` to disable coalescing for their requests.

maria_sre: I'll scoped a tenant-level override. rolling a hotspot toggle — target start in 10m, verify p95 on streaming.

ops-bot: deploy-started: toggle/stream_early_flush/tenant:acme by maria_sre at 2543212500

samir_engineer: for longer term we should: 1) add adaptive flush that considers `Accept` and `stream` flags 2) add a passive detector to apply low-latency path for clients that care about first chunk 3) update dashboard with streaming TTFB metric by tenant.

amy_devex: can we also add a sample client-side header suggestion in docs: `Prefer: early-flush` or similar, so customers can opt-in.

jordan_rt: triage notes: root cause = proxy coalescing window increase in last edge deploy. impact vector = streaming clients where early first-chunk is critical. p95 regression magnitude matches the new flush window.

devops_oncall: I've applied the tenant override and Acme reports immediate improvement: p95 down from ~900ms -> ~160ms. marking incident as mitigated. leaving deploy rollback as fallback if other tenants see regressions.

liam_support: customer confirmed UX recovered. created internal ticket RW-3842 to track adaptive-flush work + metrics.

samir_engineer: follow-ups: PR to add heuristic + feature flag, update canary dashboard, and add e2e test that simulates SSE/TCP coalescing. I'll take owner.

amy_devex: will draft docs blurb and suggest interim client workaround.

maria_sre: closing loop with postmortem template and uptime impact numbers. thanks team :thumbsup:

liam_support: thanks all — I notified Acme and will keep the thread updated if they see any regression.

(attachments: links to grafana panels, logs, and the tenant toggle runbook were posted in thread)
